items.title: Can Mechanistic Interpretability Help Explain LLM Agent Failures? A Case Study on Web Element Hallucination
items.abstract: This paper investigates whether Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) can explain LLM agent failures, specifically focusing on web agents hallucinating actions. The study applies MI to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, finding that a linear probe on the last prompt token can predict hallucinations and steering along this probe direction can correct many, though not all, errors. The contribution lies in demonstrating MI's potential for agent failure analysis while highlighting its limitations, such as sensitivity to prompt formatting, in providing a complete explanation.

items.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
items.abstract: Gamer is a generalist foundation model designed for long-horizon, real-time game agents. Its core method involves an end-to-end architecture for perception, memory, and reasoning, trained on extensive device-level interaction data and fine-tuned with sparse-thinking to reduce computation. The key contribution is its ability to operate across diverse 2D and 3D environments with a unified training and deployment pipeline, effectively handling complex, multi-step decision-making.
items.figure_caption: Overview of Gamer. A generalist game agent framework operates across a broad range of visually and mechanically diverse games. At each step, the agent uses the current screen, task context, recent interaction history, long-term memory, and reasoning to generate native keyboard and mouse actions in real time. The agent interacts continuously through this loop. Cross-game training, multi-level supervision, and persistent memory support transferable control and sustained task execution.

items.title: Personalization of Basic and Moral Values Guiding LLM-Controlled Assistant Robots
items.abstract: This paper proposes a method for personalizing the values of LLM-controlled assistant robots, moving beyond a one-size-fits-all approach. By surveying users on their own values and desired robot values, the study found that individuals often prefer robots with different, less self-focused value profiles. The contribution lies in demonstrating the feasibility and desirability of personalized robot value systems, using established psychometric tools and benchmarking current LLMs against these profiles.

items.title: Alignment by Socialization: Learning Tradeoffs Under Selection
items.abstract: This paper proposes "socialization" as a method for aligning AI agents with human values. The core idea is to use evolutionary selection, where agents reproduce based on rewarded actions, to learn complex tradeoffs between task completion and adherence to conduct rules. The contribution lies in demonstrating that this socialization process allows agents to converge to human-like decision-making and become robust to subsequent pressures that might otherwise disrupt this alignment.

items.title: ARCHER: From Rationale Imitation to Executable Reasoning in Small Language Models
items.abstract: ARCHER trains small language models for reliable mathematical reasoning by converting free-form explanations into structured, executable action traces. This framework shifts training from imitating text to learning a tool-grounded policy, enhanced by hierarchical reinforcement learning for improved performance and auditable reasoning.
items.figure_caption: Overview of ARCHER. Modules in Blue are trainable components, Light Gray are non-trainable or deterministic, Orange are Reward or evaluation, and Green are Data/traces/observations.

items.title: Black-Box Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models via Ensemble-of-Ensembles
items.abstract: This paper introduces a novel black-box method for quantifying uncertainty in Large Language Models (LLMs) by using a two-level ensemble. The core technique involves stochastic decoding of a prompt and semantic perturbations of the prompt, measuring variability in an embedding space to decompose uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components. This approach provides a computationally feasible way to distinguish prompt ambiguity from knowledge gaps, a significant contribution for reliable LLM deployment.
items.figure_caption: Two-level ensemble pipeline. (A) Localized semantic perturbation: snap noisy query embeddings to nearest of K pool K_{\( \mathrm{pool} \)} cached paraphrases ( N N times → \( \to \) outer ensemble). (B) Per-prompt M M stochastic decodes; embedding-space statistics ( μ ^ i , Σ ^ i ) (\( \hat{\mu}_{i} \),\( \hat{\Sigma}_{i} \)) feed the law-of-total-covariance AU/EU/TU split.

items.title: CoPre-MoE: Consolidating and Preserving MoE for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
items.abstract: CoPre-MoE addresses catastrophic forgetting in multimodal continual instruction tuning by introducing a novel approach to Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures. It consolidates and preserves MoE parameters by learning task-specific experts and then merging redundant expert functions into a shared set, thereby reducing parameter growth and cross-task redundancy while maintaining performance.

items.title: Do Verifier Judgments Survive Abstraction? Measuring Verification Transport for LLM Agent Evaluation
items.abstract: This paper introduces "Verification Transport," a method to assess how reliably LLM verifiers maintain their judgments when the observed execution data is altered. The core method involves creating different "views" of the same agent execution (native, abstracted, and restored) to see if the verifier's evaluation remains consistent. The key contribution is demonstrating that verifier judgments often fail to "transport" across these abstraction boundaries, highlighting a significant reliability issue in current LLM agent evaluation.
items.figure_caption: The same underlying agent execution is evaluated under native and abstracted observability. A native-correct judgment that becomes incorrect or unusable under the abstracted view constitutes a Verification Transport failure.

items.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
items.abstract: This paper introduces "agentic robotics," a new paradigm where foundation models, like GPT-6 Astra, are used to control robots in open-world tasks. The core method involves a closed-loop system that observes, reasons, acts, and verifies, moving beyond task-specific policies. The main contribution is proposing "Embodied System 2" as the decision-making core and highlighting the challenge of translating general reasoning into verifiable physical actions.

items.title: Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: This paper introduces Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (IBMARL) to improve cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning. It leverages Round-Robin Behavior Cloning (R2BC) for demonstrations and combines imitation and RL policies for each agent. An ensemble of critics then selects the best action combination, guided by a gated imitation penalty, to enhance learning efficiency and performance.

items.title: Interactive Program Induction with Language Model Priors
items.abstract: This paper addresses the ambiguity in program induction by using language model priors to guide the process. The core method is an interactive approach where the learner strategically selects inputs to query an oracle (like a user) for outputs. This interactive feedback, combined with the language model's prior knowledge, helps to efficiently narrow down the possibilities and recover the target program.

items.title: ModHarness-RL: Recasting Harnesses as Learnable and Evolving Programs for Agentic RL
items.abstract: ModHarness-RL introduces a novel approach to agentic reinforcement learning by treating the harness as a learnable and evolving program. Instead of a fixed, hand-written scaffold, ModHarness-RL dynamically generates and refines programs that manage the agent's context (Compression) and provide guidance (Steering) based on its interactions. This allows the harness to adapt to the changing needs of the agent during training, leading to more effective learning.

items.title: Right Token, Right Time: From Per-Token Gating to Trajectory-Aware Activation Steering
items.abstract: This paper introduces a new method for controlling large language models called "trajectory-aware activation steering." Instead of applying steering signals to every token, it intelligently selects specific tokens to modify, treating this selection as an allocation problem. This approach aims to improve control and preserve generation quality by steering the model's behavior at the most impactful moments.

items.title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
items.abstract: This paper introduces **WeightBench**, a novel benchmark for evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) in **Weight-Space Programming (WSP)**. WSP allows LLMs to directly manipulate neural network parameters without gradient descent. WeightBench comprises 42 tasks across five categories, testing LLMs' ability to read, fix, and write network weights, identify impossible edits, and perform data-free compression on networks of varying sizes. The contribution lies in systematically exploring and quantifying LLMs' nascent capabilities in this new paradigm, revealing current strengths and limitations.

items.title: Who Should Be on the Panel? Task-Conditioned Persona Selection for LLM Trading Agents
items.abstract: This paper proposes **task-conditioned persona selection** for LLM multi-agent systems, moving beyond fixed agent casts. Their contribution is **FinPanel**, a trading system where a recruiter dynamically selects a panel of trader personas based on a stock's trading characteristics for each new task. This allows for specialized trading strategies tailored to individual stocks.

items.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
items.abstract: This paper introduces a method to train open-weight reasoning models to control real robots using reinforcement learning entirely within simulation. Their contribution is the Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics (PEAR) and robot-use reinforcement learning (RURL) framework, which enables models to learn robot manipulation skills without real-world demonstrations, achieving generalization to unseen robots and environments.

items.title: Dancing Tokens on the Vocabulary Network from LLM Generation
items.abstract: This paper introduces a method to visualize LLM generation by mapping generated tokens onto a "vocabulary network" built from token embeddings. The core contribution is demonstrating that LLM knowledge space, learned during pre-training, is largely deterministic and structured as a scale-free, fragmented network. Generation, however, is not a simple walk on this network, but rather a concentrated exploration within its structure.

items.title: Experts Across Schemas: Agent-Guided Mixture-of-Relational-Experts for Cross-Database Generalization
items.abstract: This paper introduces MoREGT, a graph transformer that treats database rows and cells as tokens, incorporating relational features like row ages and foreign-key names. It uniquely routes data to specialized "experts" based on column metadata, not values. A novel LLM agent augments the model by generating useful derived columns from schema information alone, enabling strong cross-database generalization with significantly less pretraining data.

items.title: From Bytes to Behavior: Request-Level Attribution from Live GPU Hidden States
items.abstract: This paper introduces a novel method to extract per-layer activations from a live GPU process running a large language model. By using a non-modifying debugger and tracking tensor allocations, it bypasses the need for model architecture or weight knowledge. This allows for detailed analysis of a running LLM's behavior without interrupting or altering its operation, a significant advancement for live system forensics.

items.title: MeReader: An Offline, Privacy-Preserving, Progress-Aware AI Assistant for Narrative eBook Reading
items.abstract: MeReader is an offline, privacy-preserving AI assistant that enhances eBook reading by providing contextual AI support without risking spoilers. Its core method involves a hybrid retrieval architecture and local LLMs, ensuring responses are tied to the reader's exact position in the text. The contribution lies in demonstrating that mid-sized local models can achieve comparable comprehension to larger ones while maintaining privacy and responsiveness.

items.title: All AI-generated code should be Open Source
items.summary: The author argues that all AI-generated code should be open-source to foster transparency, collaboration, and prevent proprietary lock-in.

items.title: Qwen4-Max
items.summary: Qwen4-Max is a powerful new large language model from Alibaba, boasting enhanced reasoning, coding, and multilingual capabilities.

items.title: How to make almost anything
items.summary: This MIT course, "How to Make Almost Anything," teaches participants to design and fabricate digital creations using a wide range of tools and technologies.

items.title: Understanding Positional Embeddings in Modern LLMs
items.summary: This article explains how positional embeddings allow large language models to understand the order of words in a sequence, crucial for their performance.

items.title: Tor Project Issues Rapid-Response DoS-Defense Fix Amid Sustained DDoS Attack
items.summary: The Tor Project released a rapid fix to defend against a sustained distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack that was impacting network performance.

items.description: Build your own AI office with Univer Office SDK. Bring editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing into your product for people and AI agents. Built on an extensible open-source core.
items.summary: Univer Office SDK enables developers to integrate AI-powered office functionalities like editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing into their products for both humans and AI agents, built on an extensible open-source core.

items.description: AG-UI: the Agent-User Interaction Protocol. Bring Agents into Frontend Applications.
items.summary: AG-UI enables frontend applications to integrate agents by providing a protocol for agent-user interaction, facilitating dynamic and intelligent user experiences.

items.description: A library of Agent Skills designed to work with the Stitch MCP server. Each skill follows the Agent Skills open standard, for compatibility with coding agents such as Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Cursor.
items.summary: This repository provides a library of Agent Skills, adhering to an open standard, designed to enhance coding agents like Antigravity and Gemini CLI by enabling them to interact with the Stitch MCP server.

items.description: The workspace to stay in the loop and on top of agents - shape, decide, plan, annotate, review code, share with team, and send all feedback to agents with one click.
items.summary: Plannotator is a collaborative workspace for managing AI agents, enabling users to shape, decide, plan, annotate, review code, and share feedback seamlessly with their team and agents.

This repository provides Chrome DevTools specifically designed to assist and debug coding agents, offering features for introspection, control, and analysis of their execution within the browser environment.

items.description: Secure, fast, efficient, battle-tested at Alibaba's scale. Hybrid architecture code review tool: deterministic pipelines + LLM Agent, precise line-level comments, built-in multi-language ruleset (NPE, thread-safety, XSS, SQL injection), OpenAI & Anthropic compatible.
items.summary: This repository provides a secure, fast, and efficient hybrid code review tool for large-scale use, combining deterministic pipelines with LLM agents for precise, multi-language security and quality checks.

items.description: Self-hosted workflows for coding-agent delivery. Orchestrate CodeBuddy, Codex and Claude Code with scripts and human approval gates. Includes Local workflows for coding assistants.
items.summary: LoopForge enables self-hosted delivery of coding agents like CodeBuddy, Codex, and Claude Code through orchestrated local workflows, script execution, and human approval gates.
GGML is a C tensor library designed for efficient machine learning, featuring high performance on CPUs and GPUs, quantization support, and a focus on small, portable models.

items.description: A Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work - 82 skills, 15 slash commands, 681 disclosed-report patterns curated across 24 core vulnerability classes, plus enterprise identity + infrastructure attack matrices.
items.summary: This Claude Code skill bundle empowers bug hunters and red-teamers with 82 skills, 15 slash commands, and extensive vulnerability patterns across 24 classes, including enterprise identity and infrastructure attack matrices.

papers.title: ARCHER: From Rationale Imitation to Executable Reasoning in Small Language Models
papers.abstract: ARCHER trains small language models for reliable mathematical reasoning by converting free-form explanations into structured, executable action traces. This framework shifts training from imitating text to learning a tool-grounded policy, enhanced by hierarchical reinforcement learning for improved performance and auditable reasoning.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of ARCHER. Modules in Blue are trainable components, Light Gray are non-trainable or deterministic, Orange are Reward or evaluation, and Green are Data/traces/observations.

papers.title: Black-Box Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models via Ensemble-of-Ensembles
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel black-box method for quantifying uncertainty in Large Language Models (LLMs) by using a two-level ensemble. The core technique involves stochastic decoding of a prompt and semantic perturbations of the prompt, measuring variability in an embedding space to decompose uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components. This approach provides a computationally feasible way to distinguish prompt ambiguity from knowledge gaps, a significant contribution for reliable LLM deployment.
papers.figure_caption: Two-level ensemble pipeline. (A) Localized semantic perturbation: snap noisy query embeddings to nearest of K pool K_{\( \mathrm{pool} \)} cached paraphrases ( N N times → \( \to \) outer ensemble). (B) Per-prompt M M stochastic decodes; embedding-space statistics ( μ ^ i , Σ ^ i ) (\( \hat{\mu}_{i} \),\( \hat{\Sigma}_{i} \)) feed the law-of-total-covariance AU/EU/TU split.

papers.title: CoPre-MoE: Consolidating and Preserving MoE for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
papers.abstract: CoPre-MoE addresses catastrophic forgetting in multimodal continual instruction tuning by introducing a novel approach to Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures. It consolidates and preserves MoE parameters by learning task-specific experts and then merging redundant expert functions into a shared set, thereby reducing parameter growth and cross-task redundancy while maintaining performance.

papers.title: Do Verifier Judgments Survive Abstraction? Measuring Verification Transport for LLM Agent Evaluation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "Verification Transport," a method to assess how reliably LLM verifiers maintain their judgments when the observed execution data is altered. The core method involves creating different "views" of the same agent execution (native, abstracted, and restored) to see if the verifier's evaluation remains consistent. The key contribution is demonstrating that verifier judgments often fail to "transport" across these abstraction boundaries, highlighting a significant reliability issue in current LLM agent evaluation.
papers.figure_caption: The same underlying agent execution is evaluated under native and abstracted observability. A native-correct judgment that becomes incorrect or unusable under the abstracted view constitutes a Verification Transport failure.

papers.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "agentic robotics," a new paradigm where foundation models, like GPT-6 Astra, are used to control robots in open-world tasks. The core method involves a closed-loop system that observes, reasons, acts, and verifies, moving beyond task-specific policies. The main contribution is proposing "Embodied System 2" as the decision-making core and highlighting the challenge of translating general reasoning into verifiable physical actions.

papers.title: Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (IBMARL) to improve cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning. It leverages Round-Robin Behavior Cloning (R2BC) for demonstrations and combines imitation and RL policies for each agent. An ensemble of critics then selects the best action combination, guided by a gated imitation penalty, to enhance learning efficiency and performance.

papers.title: Interactive Program Induction with Language Model Priors
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the ambiguity in program induction by using language model priors to guide the process. The core method is an interactive approach where the learner strategically selects inputs to query an oracle (like a user) for outputs. This interactive feedback, combined with the language model's prior knowledge, helps to efficiently narrow down the possibilities and recover the target program.

papers.title: ModHarness-RL: Recasting Harnesses as Learnable and Evolving Programs for Agentic RL
papers.abstract: ModHarness-RL introduces a novel approach to agentic reinforcement learning by treating the harness as a learnable and evolving program. Instead of a fixed, hand-written scaffold, ModHarness-RL dynamically generates and refines programs that manage the agent's context (Compression) and provide guidance (Steering) based on its interactions. This allows the harness to adapt to the changing needs of the agent during training, leading to more effective learning.

papers.title: Right Token, Right Time: From Per-Token Gating to Trajectory-Aware Activation Steering
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a new method for controlling large language models called "trajectory-aware activation steering." Instead of applying steering signals to every token, it intelligently selects specific tokens to modify, treating this selection as an allocation problem. This approach aims to improve control and preserve generation quality by steering the model's behavior at the most impactful moments.

papers.title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
papers.abstract: This paper introduces **WeightBench**, a novel benchmark for evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) in **Weight-Space Programming (WSP)**. WSP allows LLMs to directly manipulate neural network parameters without gradient descent. WeightBench comprises 42 tasks across five categories, testing LLMs' ability to read, fix, and write network weights, identify impossible edits, and perform data-free compression on networks of varying sizes. The contribution lies in systematically exploring and quantifying LLMs' nascent capabilities in this new paradigm, revealing current strengths and limitations.

papers.title: Who Should Be on the Panel? Task-Conditioned Persona Selection for LLM Trading Agents
papers.abstract: This paper proposes **task-conditioned persona selection** for LLM multi-agent systems, moving beyond fixed agent casts. Their contribution is **FinPanel**, a trading system where a recruiter dynamically selects a panel of trader personas based on a stock's trading characteristics for each new task. This allows for specialized trading strategies tailored to individual stocks.

papers.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a method to train open-weight reasoning models to control real robots using reinforcement learning entirely within simulation. Their contribution is the Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics (PEAR) and robot-use reinforcement learning (RURL) framework, which enables models to learn robot manipulation skills without real-world demonstrations, achieving generalization to unseen robots and environments.

papers.title: Dancing Tokens on the Vocabulary Network from LLM Generation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a method to visualize LLM generation by mapping generated tokens onto a "vocabulary network" built from token embeddings. The core contribution is demonstrating that LLM knowledge space, learned during pre-training, is largely deterministic and structured as a scale-free, fragmented network. Generation, however, is not a simple walk on this network, but rather a concentrated exploration within its structure.

papers.title: Experts Across Schemas: Agent-Guided Mixture-of-Relational-Experts for Cross-Database Generalization
papers.abstract: This paper introduces MoREGT, a graph transformer that treats database rows and cells as tokens, incorporating relational features like row ages and foreign-key names. It uniquely routes data to specialized "experts" based on column metadata, not values. A novel LLM agent augments the model by generating useful derived columns from schema information alone, enabling strong cross-database generalization with significantly less pretraining data.

papers.title: From Bytes to Behavior: Request-Level Attribution from Live GPU Hidden States
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel method to extract per-layer activations from a live GPU process running a large language model. By using a non-modifying debugger and tracking tensor allocations, it bypasses the need for model architecture or weight knowledge. This allows for detailed analysis of a running LLM's behavior without interrupting or altering its operation, a significant advancement for live system forensics.

papers.title: MeReader: An Offline, Privacy-Preserving, Progress-Aware AI Assistant for Narrative eBook Reading
papers.abstract: MeReader is an offline, privacy-preserving AI assistant that enhances eBook reading by providing contextual AI support without risking spoilers. Its core method involves a hybrid retrieval architecture and local LLMs, ensuring responses are tied to the reader's exact position in the text. The contribution lies in demonstrating that mid-sized local models can achieve comparable comprehension to larger ones while maintaining privacy and responsiveness.
